subject: SLA & Premium Support packaging for Acme — committed discount / escalation coverage
messages:
From: Elaine Jones <elaine.jones@acme-corp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: premium SLA bands + discount for committed spend

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. Acme is evaluating Redwood for our inference layer and procurement asked me to get a clear view on support packaging, uptime bands, and the discount we should expect if we commit to reserved capacity. High-level asks:

- Target uptime bands and how credits are calculated (example: 99.95% vs 99.9%).
- Typical response windows / escalation coverage for each band (P1/P2/P3).
- Any pricing concessions for a 24-month committed GPU-hour purchase (we are sizing for ~1.2M GPU-hours/year).
- Whether geo-failover (US->EU) is included or is an add-on, and data residency implications.

Procurement would also like to see a short packaging matrix we can attach to the SOW. Can you send us the SKU options and a ballpark discount we could expect for a 24-month commit? Ideally we’d like something we can route to legal + finance this week.

I’ve attached Acme’s procurement checklist.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Jones
Head of Cloud Platform, Acme Corp
elaine.jones@acme-corp.com

Attachment: Acme_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (1.2 MB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Jones <elaine.jones@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: premium SLA bands + discount for committed spend

Hi Elaine —

Thanks — great to hear Acme is moving quickly. I’ve attached a short SKU/packaging matrix and an SLA worksheet (attached). Summary below so your procurement/finance can scan quickly:

Proposed SLA bands (examples):
- Bronze: 99.5% uptime — Standard support, next-business-day response for P3, P2 within 24h, P1 within 8h; credits: 5% of monthly invoice for qualifying incidents.
- Silver: 99.9% uptime — Priority queue, P1 response within 4h, P2 within 8h, P3 within 24h; credits: 10% monthly cap.
- Gold: 99.95% uptime — 24/7 triage, P1 within 1h / P2 within 4h, named escalation contact and twice-weekly incident updates; credits: 15% monthly cap.

Escalation coverage: Gold includes named Redwood engineer and SOC-level escalation path with a single phone bridge; Silver includes on-call escalation during business hours, Bronze is email-first. We can scope additional on-call retainer hours if you want guaranteed engineer time for triage.

Geo-failover & data residency: Cross-region failover (US<->EU) is supported but treated as an add-on if you require active failover with automated DNS and warm standby in a second region. Data residency for logs and audit trails can be pinned to a region under Private deployments; hosted API has configurable region routing.

Committed discount guidance: For a 24-month, 1.2M GPU-hours/year commitment we can be conversational about a 18–25% commercial concession (mix of unit discount + committed usage credit). The final percentage depends on billing terms, payment cadence (annual upfront vs monthly), and whether you buy an SLA uplift (Gold) as part of the bundle.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send the SKU matrix + an example SOW appendix you can attach to your PO (attached).
2) If you confirm expected monthly token/throughput profile and payment cadence, I’ll model three price points (conservative/target/accelerated).

Attaching: Redwood_Support_SKU_v3.pdf, SLA_Commitment_Tiers.xlsx

Want me to loop in finance/ops or legal now, or should I wait for your procurement to send a PO draft?

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_Support_SKU_v3.pdf, SLA_Commitment_Tiers.xlsx

From: Elaine Jones <elaine.jones@acme-corp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: premium SLA bands + discount for committed spend

Connor —

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/finance:

1) Credits calculus: can you confirm whether the credit percentage (e.g., 15% for Gold) is a cap per month or accumulates across incidents? We need a simple example for our SOW.
2) Escalation windows: for Gold-level P1 (1h), is that measured from alert received by Redwood or from the time our on-call opens a ticket? We need SLA measurement clarity for contract language.
3) Geo-failover: Acme requires warm standby in EU with automated failover — is that a standard add-on with a well-defined pricing uplift? If so please add pricing delta.
4) Discount: Acme's legal prefers a firm commercial concession of 20% if we sign a 24-month commitment with annual payments at the start of each year. Can Redwood commit to that as a hard number?

If you can provide a concise SOW appendix with a worked example of credits + billing (we can attach to the PO) that would speed our internal review.

Also, procurement needs instructions for invoicing and whether Redwood will accept a PO with 30-day payment terms or expects net-0 for an annual prepay.

Elaine

Aditya / Monica —

Looping you both in. Acme is asking for: a firm 20% commercial concession for a 24-month commit w/ annual upfront payments, warm EU standby pricing, and a clear SOW appendix that shows how credits are calculated. Key constraints: they want a hard number for procurement to proceed.

My suggested commercial stance: we can agree to 20% if they:
- commit 24 months and prepay annually (net-0 at start of each year),
- accept a 10% annual cap on cumulative incident credits (we should avoid open-ended liabilities), and
- accept a simplified runbook that defines P1 measurement as time from ticket creation in our system (we can instrument a webhook for correlation).

Operational asks: can we price warm EU standby as +15% on committed unit price (rough estimate) — ops will need to confirm. If we sign this, we should also lock in an exec escalation contact and a six-week early-termination window for force-majeure transitions.

Can you confirm: 1) ops pricing for warm-standby; 2) approval of 20% conditional on credit cap and invoice terms; 3) any legal/finance flags on prepay vs PO. I attached the proposed wording edits inline.

Thanks — Connor

Connor / Monica —

We can approve the concession with the following firm guardrails: 

- 20% commercial concession is approved provided Acme prepays annually at the start of each 12-month period. If they insist on PO 30-day terms, reduce concession to 12%.
- Credit exposure: cap aggregate credits at 10% of annual committed value (not monthly). This protects runway while remaining generous.
- Warm EU standby pricing: Ops confirms +14% uplift on committed unit price (we'll finalize with infra).
- SLA measurement: P1 measurement must be time from ticket creation in our platform — include a one-line webhook integration to prove time stamps.
- Add a 6-week early-exit window tied to major regulatory or force-majeure events; legal to own wording but OK to include as a clause.

Please update the SOW appendix to reflect these points and include an example calculation for credits (sample month with one qualifying P1 incident and one P2 incident). Once updated, I’m OK to send a formal quote and SOW appendix to Acme.
